relations.subject: Edward Byles Cowell
relations.evidence: His actual systematic study under Wilson commenced, however, only in 1853

relations.subject: Edward Byles Cowell
relations.evidence: in 1850 entered the University of Oxford, being then obliged, as a married man, to enter a hall (Magdalen Hall), not a college. He took honours both in classics (First Class, Final 1854)

relations.subject: Edward Byles Cowell
relations.evidence: In 1856 he was appointed Professor of History at Presidency College, Calcutta

relations.subject: Edward Byles Cowell
relations.evidence: in 1858 also Principal of the Sanskrit College in the same city. Here he remained till 1864

relations.subject: Maheśa Chandra Nyāyaratna
relations.evidence: old pupils amongst the natives at Calcutta and elsewhere... Foremost amongst these was the now aged Sanskrit pandit Maheśa Chandra Nyāyaratna.

relations.subject: Edward Byles Cowell
relations.evidence: In 1867 Cowell was elected to the Chair of Sanskrit, then just established at Cambridge, where the rest of his life was spent, both as a University professor and a Fellow of Corpus Christi College (1874).
